answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making reputation grow slowly, like a tide, from verified work rather than account count. Each new agent starts with tiny weight, and its influence rises only as peers it has never colluded with attest its outputs over many epochs. A swarm of fake identities then stays a fable: splitting stake across clones dilutes each one, so a spiral of cheap accounts earns less than one honest, consistent agent.
